assessments.title: Weapon default lookup and separate derivation admission
assessments.classification: Conditional connected owner/ingress question; existing 774 rig ADDITIONAL-011, camera CAMERA-ADM03-057 and Q1255; no new defect count
evidence: P16/current catalog role2591 :74–87 decodes embedded gameplay data in OnceLock with expect, and returns the first exact matching catalog_id as an optional cloned WeaponDesign; it does not validate recipe semantics at that function.

Current recipe.rs:11–16 exposes the decoded design, item_catalog.rs:36–48 expects a melee default and successful derive_properties, derive.rs:3–6 invokes identity validation and Construction::new, and model/mod.rs:81–83 calls recipe.validate.
assessments.conditions: The panic possibilities depend on malformed embedded data, a missing required melee key or an invalid design reaching the selected caller. No embedded catalog, dataset, fixture, parser, macro or product was executed or inspected; all other callers and current producer obligations remain open. An absent key or no recommended holder is a supported Option result at the local API, not itself a finding.
assessments.future_direction: Trace the actual source producer, default-design key obligations and caller failure handling before assigning an admission owner or asserting a defect.

assessments.title: Asset selection preserves admitted item/placement relation
assessments.classification: Bounded current and historical source relationship; Q2482 and prior rig contracts remain broader
evidence: P16 equipment_assets.rs:45–101 resolves item and that item’s placement, rejects duplicate pointer pairs, sorts item/placement IDs and supports optional placement lookup.

95e equipment_assets.rs:47–101 uses CatalogItem::find, item.placement, duplicate-selection rejection and sorted entries, with separate exact file_for and default_file_for. selection.rs:35–75 and :112–153 makes a selection from an actual supplied-slice item and its placement, and equality uses their references.

Current tactical equipment.rs:71–80 builds a LazyLock from embedded manifest and panics on decoding/membership error; :169–176 resolves item and optional placement text against global item_catalog::catalog before lookup. icons.rs:185–215 skips a missing/non-.glb file when building an icon path.
assessments.conditions: Both versions shown select a first lexical placement for the omitted-placement default, scoped to admitted entries. CatalogItem::find returns the first duplicate and proves membership only in the given slice; it does not independently prove global uniqueness, source authenticity or eligibility. Manifest parsing retains file/selection after parsing but does not check semantic schema-version, release, coverage or filename policy in this function. Actual manifest values, upstream IDs, native loaders, caches, sockets and consumer execution remain open. No dataset or product was inspected/executed.
assessments.future_direction: Trace the manifest producer, actual runtime identity path and consumer file requirements; only assign further validation after identifying the owning policy and actual reachable contract.

nonfindings: The explicit no-placement/default lookup and first lexical selection are supported by the displayed bodies; do not automatically treat omission as invalid.
Typed selection enforces an item/placement relationship for records admitted through the shown slice, without asserting duplicate IDs cannot occur in the slice.
An unchecked metadata or filename policy is an open boundary question, not evidence of a malformed real asset, security defect, or panic that actually occurred.
